forces: Concert band, arranged by Thomas Knox
performers: United States Marine Band; Col John R. Bourgeois
intro: The United States Marine Band, conducted by John R. Bourgeois, plays Thomas Knox’s concert-band arrangement of Kashchei’s Infernal Dance from The Firebird. In the ballet the dance is the Firebird’s spell on the sorcerer and his creatures.
license: Public domain in the US (US Marine Band recording; composition published 1910)

cues.title: Infernal Dance, scenario
cues.text: In the ballet scenario, the Firebird enchants Kashchei and his subjects into an infernal dance. The music is built from short, angular phrases that break off and start again.
cues.evidence: The ballet scenario describes the Firebird enchanting Kashchei and his subjects into an infernal dance: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Firebird. Marcel Bowman, The Human Versus the Supernatural, pp. 98–99, discusses the dance’s angular motifs: https://collections.lib.utah.edu/dl_files/6e/34/6e3433faa6efb79c80229fe8373f0a7d3aaeab9c.pdf.
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Semitone and tritone motifs
cues.text: The tune moves by semitones between neighbouring notes, then jumps a tritone. Bowman traced these two motifs through rehearsal figures 133–141 and 161 of the ballet score.
cues.evidence: Bowman, The Human Versus the Supernatural, pp. 98–99, examples 45a–e, traces the semitone and tritone motifs through rehearsal figures 133–141 and 161 of the ballet score: https://collections.lib.utah.edu/dl_files/6e/34/6e3433faa6efb79c80229fe8373f0a7d3aaeab9c.pdf.
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: First performance, Paris Opéra, 1910
cues.text: On 25 June 1910 Tamara Karsavina danced the Firebird at the Paris Opéra. Michel Fokine provided the choreography for Diaghilev’s Ballets Russes. Stravinsky was twenty-eight.
cues.evidence: The premiere date, theatre, company, choreographer and original Firebird are documented at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Firebird. Stravinsky’s birth on 17 June 1882 is documented by the Fondation Igor Stravinsky: https://fondation-igor-stravinsky.org/en/composer/biography/.

cues.title: Four-note descending motif
cues.text: One of Kashchei’s recurring motifs descends chromatically through four neighbouring notes, as at rehearsal figures 141 and 160. The fragment is short and passes easily from one phrase to another. It is heard alongside Kashchei’s wide leaps.
cues.evidence: Bowman, The Human Versus the Supernatural, pp. 103–05, examples 49 and 52, identifies the descending four-note chromatic motif at rehearsal figures 141 and 160 of the Infernal Dance. This note describes a recurring motif, not a single entrance: https://collections.lib.utah.edu/dl_files/6e/34/6e3433faa6efb79c80229fe8373f0a7d3aaeab9c.pdf.
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Stravinsky as “Mr. Fireberg”
cues.text: In Expositions and Developments, his 1962 book with Robert Craft, Stravinsky recalled a stranger in an American railway dining car who addressed him as “Mr. Fireberg”. He did not date the encounter.
cues.evidence: Igor Stravinsky and Robert Craft, Expositions and Developments (1962), passage on The Firebird, quoted in Marcel Bowman, The Human Versus the Supernatural, p. 4: https://collections.lib.utah.edu/dl_files/6e/34/6e3433faa6efb79c80229fe8373f0a7d3aaeab9c.pdf. The recollection does not date the encounter.

composer.born: 17 June 1882, Oranienbaum, near St Petersburg, Russia
composer.epithet: Composer of dance music in which a single displaced accent could unsettle the dancers, and of a psalm setting that scarcely moves.
facts: Diaghilev’s Ballets Russes · Ramuz’s travelling theatre · Balanchine · Auden and Kallman
Ballets, operas, symphonies and sacred music; composing and recording into his eighties
composer.background:
Stravinsky was born in 1882 at Oranienbaum. His father, Fyodor, sang bass at the Mariinsky Theatre in St Petersburg; Igor heard him on stage and began piano lessons at nine. He entered St Petersburg University to study law. There he befriended Vladimir Rimsky-Korsakov, whose father heard his first pieces in 1902. Rimsky-Korsakov took him on privately, giving regular lessons from 1905 until his death in 1908. The pupil orchestrated pages of Pan Voyevoda, then had to explain why his teacher had scored them differently.

He married his cousin Catherine Nossenko in 1906; by 1914 they had four children. His E♭ Symphony owed much to Glazunov and Tchaikovsky; Scherzo fantastique and Fireworks are short orchestral works. Sergei Diaghilev heard his music in 1909 and gave him some Chopin to orchestrate for Les Sylphides. A full ballet, The Firebird, followed. Stravinsky handed over the score in sections while Michel Fokine worked out the dances. In his 1936 autobiography he recalled that the rehearsals ended with dinner beside Diaghilev and Nijinsky, and good claret.
